text:
sarah_support: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting p95/p99 regressions on text-generation endpoint over the past hour. They see long queueing delays and 429-ish admission throttles. Any recent deploys?
alex_runtime: Not that I deployed. I see a small config push at 1718001000 related to auth cache TTL. Could be related.
priya_sre: Observed a burst of `admit_queue_wait_ms` at ~1718003000 in prod. Spike correlates with increased auth lookup latency to the token service (auth-db).
maya_custsuccess: ACME and BetaCorp both sent repro traces — users hit delays ~600-900ms extra end-to-end; they call our /v1/generate concurrently.
tom_oncall: I can confirm the ingress admission queueing increased. Per-route concurrency caps tripped and we started fast-failing. See snippet from logs:```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","tenant":"acme","admit_wait_ms":742,"errors":"admit_throttle"}
```
sarah_support: Repro steps from customer (short):
1) run 50 parallel requests: `for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done`
2) observe queueing and ~10% 503/429s after ~30s

alex_runtime: Thanks. Quick root-cause theory: auth service latency -> more request processing time in ingress -> backpressure on worker pool -> admission control trips sooner. Also saw increased retry attempts from client side amplifying load.
priya_sre: Oncall mitigation suggestions: 1) temporarily relax per-tenant low-priority concurrency floor for hosted tier (gives breathing room) 2) enable short warmup for idle workers 3) rollback auth-cache TTL change if that's the culprit.
tom_oncall: I can flip the concurrency floor for hosted tier to +20% now. Doing it in 2m and will monitor.
deploy-bot: deploy started by tom_oncall: config/ingress/concurrency-floor += 20% (id: cfg-1718004390)
alex_runtime: Also suggest patch to bounce auth cache workers with backoff and increase token lookup cache hit rate. If rollback needed I can revert config push from 1718001000.
maya_custsuccess: Let me message affected customers with ETA + ask for their request IDs so we can correlate traces.
sarah_support: Tom — after you bump floor can you post p95/p99 from observability? Want a before/after.
tom_oncall: P95 before bump: 312ms, P99: 1240ms. After bump (5m): P95: 208ms, P99: 650ms. Improvement but still above baseline.
priya_sre: Good. Next steps: 1) rollback auth cache TTL change (candidate cause) 2) add short-term per-tenant rate smoothing to reduce thundering retries 3) add an alert for auth-db latency > 150ms that auto-tags incidents.
alex_runtime: Rolling back TTL now: rolling back commit 8f2c4a (auth cache TTL change). Will keep trace sampling on for affected tenants.
deploy-bot: rollback completed (commit 8f2c4a) by alex_runtime at 1718004720
priya_sre: After rollback and smoothing, p99 trending down to ~300ms. Looks like TTL change amplified token lookup pressure.
maya_custsuccess: Updated ACME and BetaCorp with summary + mitigation steps. They appreciate quick response.
sarah_support: Capture follow-up action items: [ ] longer-term fix: token-cache sharding + per-tenant TTLs, [ ] admission-control change to prefer fairness over simple first-come, [ ] improve client guidance to reduce retries with jitter, [ ] postmortem if p99 > 500ms for >30m.
priya_sre: I'll open the incident PM and assign owners.
tom_oncall: Added temporary dashboard with per-route admit_wait_ms and auth-db latency. Will keep monitoring for 2 hours.
alex_runtime: Also: add a quick smoke test to CI that simulates auth-cache churn so we don't regress this.
sarah_support: Thanks everyone. Closing customer escalations for now; will follow-up in incident doc. :checked:
